blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Autograph Collection commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and Marriott sales systems while each hotel keeps its own design and guest narrative. Owners should underwrite channel mix and Bonvoy contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus hard brands, Autograph sells individuality plus Marriott commercial infrastructure; versus pure independents, it adds Bonvoy earn/redeem, centralized sales tools, and portfolio campaigns without collapsing the hotel into a standardized prototype.

blocks.title: Channels
blocks.body: Brand.com / Marriott Bonvoy app · major OTAs · GDS · metasearch (where active for the hotel)

blocks.title: Campaigns
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy and parent portfolio campaigns where the Autograph hotel is eligible

blocks.title: B2B Programs
blocks.body: Corporate, SME, and RFP programs routed through Marriott sales infrastructure where active for this flag

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Model Autograph contribution after loyalty chargebacks, preferred-agency commissions, and local competitive set reality—not headline RevPAR alone.

blocks.title: Demand Pattern
blocks.body: Autograph demand follows destination seasonality plus Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional; diligence this hotel's source markets and corporate vs leisure mix.

blocks.title: Competitive Pressure
blocks.body: Sibling Marriott soft brands (Tribute Portfolio, Design Hotels) and local independents can both help and cannibalize. Map same-parent density before assuming exclusive Bonvoy pull.

blocks.title: Distribution & Channel Mix
blocks.body: Marriott central reservations, Bonvoy app, and designated online channels—confirm commission structures and rate parity obligations in the current agreement exhibit.

blocks.title: Revenue Management
blocks.body: Marriott revenue tools and Bonvoy demand signals support pricing experiments; owners still need property-level strategy for distinctive Autograph product.

blocks.title: Digital Marketing & Performance Media
blocks.body: Paid and owned media templates at portfolio scale, with creative that must still feel hotel-specific rather than generic Marriott hard-brand advertising.

blocks.title: Corporate, SME & Group Pull
blocks.body: Contracted travelers, small meetings, and negotiated programs where Autograph acts as a distinctive but Bonvoy-connected option.

blocks.title: Sales & Catering
blocks.body: Marriott sales systems support group and catering leads; conversion depends on the hotel's meeting product and local sales discipline.

blocks.title: Leisure & Destination Demand
blocks.body: Story-led leisure stays and destination immersion are core Autograph use cases—pair Bonvoy leisure campaigns with credible local experience programming.

blocks.title: International Reach
blocks.body: Year-end 2025 Autograph system spanned U.S. & Canada, Europe, MEA, Asia Pacific, Greater China, and Caribbean & Latin America (Marriott 10-K). International Bonvoy demand is real but property-specific.
blocks.source: Marriott International Form 10-K for year ended Dec 31, 2025 — Autograph Collection® system properties/rooms

blocks.title: Data, Analytics & Experimentation
blocks.body: Use Marriott reporting to isolate channel and Bonvoy contribution for this Autograph asset; avoid extrapolating from sibling soft brands.

blocks.title: Reputation & QA
blocks.body: Guest reviews and brand QA surface design/F&B/service mismatches quickly on character-led hotels—budget for ongoing standards discipline.

blocks.title: Immersive Character
blocks.body: Every Autograph hotel is sold on individuality—commercial messaging must protect that story while still routing demand through Bonvoy.

blocks.title: Owner Perception Risk
blocks.body: Owners sometimes expect soft-brand lightness; Autograph still carries Marriott systems, Bonvoy economics, and design/QA expectations. Align IC expectations early.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: Autograph Collection participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating Marriott brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on marriottbonvoy.com before IC.
blocks.source: Marriott Bonvoy program participation stated on Autograph brand communications

blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy at Autograph Collection

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Autograph Collection hotels. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current Bonvoy rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including Autograph Collection hotels, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—Autograph individuality means amenity delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Bonvoy Moments, co-branded cards, and partner redemptions expand the loyalty halo; Autograph stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Systems Implications

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of second and third Autograph stays where the hotel already competes on distinctive experience—not on a standardized hard-brand prototype.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help Autograph hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping each property's individual narrative intact.

blocks.body: Elite recognition (upgrades where available, late checkout, milestone rewards) supports contribution at Autograph hotels; amenity delivery still varies by property capability and design.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: Bonvoy recognition across Marriott sister brands matters for guests who split stays within the network—Autograph remains the character-hotel node inside that earn/redeem graph.

blocks.title: Cobrand & Payment Scale
blocks.body: Bonvoy co-branded cards, Moments, and bonus-point campaigns lift acquisition and keep the program top-of-wallet; model hotel-level contribution after loyalty chargebacks—not portfolio vanity metrics.

blocks.title: Corporate & Small Meetings

blocks.title: To Join
blocks.body: Application $100,000 new-to-system / conversion (+ $400/key over 250); existing Autograph or managed-to-franchise path greater of $150,000 or $500/key; PIP / brand assessment and systems install are separate (confirm current FDD exhibits). Design, market study, and F&B concept costs vary by conversion vs new-build
blocks.source: Autograph Collection Domestic FDD issued Mar 31, 2025 (public Marriott development disclosure)

blocks.title: To Operate
blocks.body: Steady-state 5% monthly royalty on gross rooms sales; Program Services Contribution (~2.02% of GRS plus fixed annual and per-key components—confirm current exhibit); Marriott Bonvoy loyalty assessment on eligible member revenue (public FDD cites ~4.2%, with disclosed temporary reduction to 4.0% through 2027—confirm live exhibit); model owner economics after loyalty chargebacks and distribution—not headline RevPAR
blocks.source: Autograph Collection Domestic FDD issued Mar 31, 2025 (public Marriott development disclosure)

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit, not steady-state operations. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.
blocks.source: Autograph Collection Domestic FDD issued Mar 31, 2025 (public Marriott development disclosure)

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Your Independent Spirit—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain hotel individuality and local character while accessing Bonvoy earn/redeem, Marriott sales, and portfolio campaigns that a standalone boutique cannot buy on its own.
Exactly Like Nothing Else Positioning: hand-selected design-led hotels in desirable destinations—362 open properties / 76,399 rooms at year-end 2025 (Marriott 10-K)—underwrite the asset's story, not a prototype corridor.
Conversion-Ready Within Soft-Brand Economics: application and systems economics support conversion and adaptive reuse—model design, public-space, and F&B capital plus Bonvoy contribution before any term sheet.
Sibling Clarity Versus Tribute & Design Hotels: Autograph spans upper-upscale to luxury-leaning character hotels; diligence fit versus Tribute Portfolio and Design Hotels before assuming the same owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest for owners and operators who can run distinctive full-service hospitality with design QA and F&B discipline—weakest for breakfast-only limited-service seeking a Marriott flag without an independent narrative.
blocks.source: Marriott International Form 10-K for year ended Dec 31, 2025 — Autograph Collection® system properties/rooms

blocks.title: Design-Led Independent Conversion
blocks.body: Independent boutiques and heritage conversions with a credible design or narrative concept—where owners want Marriott Bonvoy distribution without erasing the property's individual identity into a hard-brand prototype.

blocks.title: Destination Lifestyle & Resort Character
blocks.body: Resorts, urban lifestyle landmarks, and destination hotels where authenticity, design, and F&B drive rate power—Autograph's flexible collection standards reward distinctive product over standardized corridors.

blocks.title: Adaptive Reuse & Landmark Adaptive Stays
blocks.body: Historic cores, landmark buildings, and adaptive reuse where architecture and sense of place are the product—pair design capital with Bonvoy commercial systems.
